articles.author: Venkatsai Nuthi
articles.description:
Building DealPilot: A Persistent Memory Sales Intelligence Agent with Groq & Hindsight


Sales representatives lose hours each week sifting through CRM notes, previous call transcripts, and stakeholder feedback. Traditional AI assistants process each call as a blank slate, leading to repeated mistakes or generic pitches. 
To solve this, I built DealPilot for the HackwithHyderabad Hackathon—a smart sales intelligence agent that uses Vectorize Hindsight for long-term persistent memory and Groq for lightning-fast inference.
When managing multi-stakeholder enterprise deals, critical context often gets forgotten:
A CFO refuses upfront discounts and prefers contract length negotiations.
An IT Security Lead blocks deals without ISO 27001 audit reports.
A VP of Operations prefers two-slide summaries over long pitch decks.
Generic AI bots give blanket advice like "offer a 10% discount to close fast," which can ruin real-world enterprise deals.
DealPilot acts as a persistent memory companion for sales reps:
Cold Start (Interaction 1): Without prior memory, the agent provides standard, baseline guidance.
Context Memory Retention (Interaction 2): As call notes and rep feedback are entered, DealPilot ingests them into Vectorize Hindsight memory banks.
Tailored Brief Generation (Interaction 3): When asked for a pre-call brief, DealPilot recalls stakeholder constraints, deal risks, and previous feedback to deliver a hyper-specific action plan.
Groq LLM API: Powers fast, low-latency reasoning and response generation.
Vectorize Hindsight Client: Provides persistent memory recall and context indexing.
Python: CLI application structure and JSON deal state management.
GitHub Repository: https://github.com/venkatsainuthi47-design/dealpilot-hindsight
articles.title: Building DealPilot: A Persistent Memory Sales Intelligence Agent with Groq & Hindsight

articles.author: kate astrid
articles.description:
We know humans have cognitive biases. They affect the way we make decisions, interpret information, and judge uncertainty.
But what about AI?
Can a language model show the same patterns? Can an irrelevant detail influence its judgment? Can the way information is presented change its answer?
Researchers have found patterns in language models that resemble several well-known cognitive biases, including anchoring, availability, representativeness, framing, and the endowment effect.
That doesn't mean AI experiences these biases in the same way humans do. A cognitive bias describes a pattern in human cognition. With AI, we're observing a pattern in its output.
But if the pattern is there, it's worth understanding.
So let's put some of these biases to the test.

articles.title: Does AI Have Cognitive Biases Too?

articles.author: William Rodriguez
articles.description:
Basta de f-strings caóticos: SQL fluido y seguro para ClickHouse.



Día 08 de la serie técnica WClickHouse Open Source.
Construir queries analíticas dinámicas uniendo f-strings es un accidente esperando ocurrir. WClickHouse QueryBuilder te da composición SQL fluida y segura.
Cadenas SQL multilínea frágiles llenas de f-strings y errores de sintaxis
Riesgos de inyección SQL por concatenar parámetros dinámicos sin escapar
Dificultad de reutilizar código al componer dashboards dinámicos con filtros
from wclickhouse import QueryBuilder

qb = QueryBuilder()
query, params = (
    qb.table("orders")
    .select(["region", "count() as total_orders", "sum(amount) as revenue"])
    .where("status = :status", status="completed")
    .where("amount > :min_amount", min_amount=100)
    .group_by(["region"])
    .having("revenue > :min_rev", min_rev=10000)
    .order_by("revenue", ascending=False)
    .limit(10)
    .build()
)

API Encadenada: Construye queries con select(), where(), group_by(), order_by().
Anti Inyección: Parámetros escapados y validados de forma transparente.
Operadores Avanzados: Soporte nativo para joins, union_all y subconsultas.
Probado y verificado contra instancias reales de ClickHouse con más de 95% de cobertura de tests. Desarrollado para Python 3.9 a 3.14 con Apache Arrow y Pydantic v2.
GitHub: https://github.com/wisrovi/wclickhouse


PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/wclickhouse




  
  
  ClickHouse #Python #DataEngineering #OLAP #BigData #Wisrovi
articles.title: Basta de f-strings caóticos: SQL fluido y seguro para ClickHouse.

articles.author: William Rodriguez
articles.description:
No more messy f-strings: Type-safe fluent SQL for ClickHouse.



Day 08 of the WClickHouse Open-Source Engineering Series.
Building dynamic analytical queries by stitching f-strings together is an accident waiting to happen. WClickHouse QueryBuilder gives you fluent, safe SQL composition.
Brittle multi-line SQL strings full of dangerous f-string formatting and syntax typos
SQL injection risks from unescaped dynamic query parameters
Difficult code reusability when composing dynamic dashboards with conditional filters
from wclickhouse import QueryBuilder

qb = QueryBuilder()
query, params = (
    qb.table("orders")
    .select(["region", "count() as total_orders", "sum(amount) as revenue"])
    .where("status = :status", status="completed")
    .where("amount > :min_amount", min_amount=100)
    .group_by(["region"])
    .having("revenue > :min_rev", min_rev=10000)
    .order_by("revenue", ascending=False)
    .limit(10)
    .build()
)

Chained API: Build queries fluently with select(), where(), group_by(), order_by().
Injection Protected: Parameters escaped and validated automatically.
Advanced Operators: Native support for joins, union_all, and subqueries.
Tested and verified against live ClickHouse server instances with 95%+ test coverage. Built for Python 3.9 through 3.14 with Apache Arrow and Pydantic v2.
GitHub: https://github.com/wisrovi/wclickhouse


PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/wclickhouse

articles.author: William Rodriguez
articles.description:
Evita que los mensajes tóxicos congelen tu pipeline: Reintentos y DLQ.



Día 08 de la serie técnica WKafka Open Source.
Un único JSON malformado jamás debería tumbar un consumidor de Kafka en producción. WKafka aísla los mensajes tóxicos en una Dead Letter Queue automáticamente.
Un único payload corrupto congelando la partición en bucles de crash infinitos
Tormentas de reintentos descontroladas saturando bases de datos aguas abajo
Pérdida de mensajes fallidos sin trazas forenses ni pistas para depurar
@kafka.consumer(
    topic="invoices",
    max_retries=3,
    retry_backoff=2.0,
    dlq_topic="invoices.DLQ"
)
def process_invoice(msg):
    # If this fails 3 times, message automatically moves to invoices.DLQ
    parse_and_bill(msg.value)

Dead Letter Queue: Enruta automáticamente los fallos permanentes a topic.DLQ.
Backoff Exponencial: Intervalos de reintento suaves evitan tormentas de peticiones.
Cero Bloqueos: Los mensajes sanos continúan procesándose mientras el error se aísla.
Probado y verificado contra clusters reales de Apache Kafka (ver EXAMPLES_STATUS.md en el repositorio). Compatible con Python 3.9 a 3.14 con tipado estricto mypy.
GitHub: https://github.com/wisrovi/wkafka


PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/wkafka




  
  
  Kafka #Python #DataEngineering #OpenSource #Wisrovi
articles.title: Evita que los mensajes tóxicos congelen tu pipeline: Reintentos y DLQ.

articles.author: William Rodriguez
articles.description:
Stop poison pills from halting your Kafka pipeline: Retries and DLQ.



Day 08 of the WKafka Open-Source Engineering Series.
A single malformed JSON payload should never bring down a production Kafka consumer. WKafka isolates poison pills into a Dead Letter Queue automatically.
A single corrupt payload blocking consumer partitions in infinite crash loops
Uncontrolled retry storms overwhelming downstream databases
Losing failed payloads without audit trails or forensic debugging traces
@kafka.consumer(
    topic="invoices",
    max_retries=3,
    retry_backoff=2.0,
    dlq_topic="invoices.DLQ"
)
def process_invoice(msg):
    # If this fails 3 times, message automatically moves to invoices.DLQ
    parse_and_bill(msg.value)

Dead Letter Queue: Automatically routes permanently failing records to topic.DLQ.
Exponential Backoff: Smooth retry intervals prevent thundering herds on recovery.
Zero Pipeline Halts: Healthy messages continue processing while errors are quarantined.
Tested and verified with Apache Kafka against real broker clusters (see EXAMPLES_STATUS.md in repository). Compatible with Python 3.9 through 3.14 with strict typing.
GitHub: https://github.com/wisrovi/wkafka


PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/wkafka
